ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a long straight wire along the vertical z direction, the current is labeled I=2 A, and the direction is upward. On the right side of the wire there is a square conducting loop; the horizontal distance between the left side of the loop and the wire is labeled d=1 m; the horizontal side length and vertical side length of the loop are both labeled a=1 m. Reasoning: Let r be the horizontal distance from the long straight wire to some vertical narrow strip inside the loop. The magnitude of the magnetic field produced by the long straight wire at distance r is B(r)=μ0 I/(2πr), with direction perpendicular to the plane of the loop. Divide the square loop into vertical narrow strips with height a and width dr, then the magnetic flux through that narrow strip is dΦ=B(r)a dr=μ0 I a/(2πr) dr. Integrate over the whole loop from r=d to r=d+a: Φ=∫_d^(d+a) μ0 I a/(2πr) dr=μ0 I a/(2π) ln((d+a)/d). The mutual inductance M=Φ/I=μ0 a/(2π) ln((d+a)/d). Substitute μ0=4π×10^-7 H/m, a=1 m, d=1 m: M=(4π×10^-7)/(2π) ln(2)=2×10^-7×0.693147=1.38629×10^-7 H. Converted to nH: 1.38629×10^-7 H = 138.629 nH, rounded to two decimal places is 138.63 nH.
